references.text: The context for the release of a servant after six years, which forms the basis for the provision regarding wife and children in verse 4
Describes the option where the servant chooses to remain with his master out of love for his wife and children
Parallel legislation concerning the release of Hebrew servants, including provisions about family relationships
Laws regarding Israelite servants and their rights, which supplement the provisions in Exodus
Laban claims ownership over his daughters and grandchildren, reflecting a similar principle that wives and children belong to the master
Jeremiah refers to the law concerning the release of Hebrew servants and criticizes violations of this covenant
Contrasting outcomes at release: Exodus shows loss of family (going alone), while Leviticus shows reunion with relatives and children.
Parallel legislation: Both verses regulate the temporary transfer of property (people/land) that is returned to the original owner in the year of release.
